distinguishing_features: Passive surface-energy modification (SLIPS liquid-infused porous layer) rather than a procedural thermal-cycling duty cycle on existing controls
Shifts failure mode from adhesion-accumulation to shear-detachment by lowering interfacial adhesion energy, rather than inducing thermal-stress spallation
No new hardware in prior art vs. etched porous substrate plus infused liquid in candidate
Self-cleaning at operating shear stress without any scheduled intervention or setpoint cycling
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent asphaltene fouling from accumulating and hardening on crude preheat train heat-transfer surfaces so that deposit is continuously removed at normal operating flow, eliminating scheduled cleaning shutdowns.
parsed.viable_reason: The SLIPS liquid layer is assumed to be replenished by the process stream itself, but a stable infused film cannot be maintained against 2 m/s crude shear and asphaltene-rich crude will wet and displace the low-surface-energy lubricant, so the self-cleaning mechanism is physically implausible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The interfacial-physics approach (liquid-infused porous surface lowering adhesion energy to enable shear detachment) is a distinct mechanism not suggested by the thermal-cycling or monitoring prior art, so it is not an obvious routine adaptation.
